# Using the Button nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-buttons.html#using-the-button-nodes "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Use the Button nodes to create interactions through clicking, tapping, or pressing a key on the keyboard.
Use Button 3D to create a 3D button and Button 2D to create a 2D button.
Kanzi allows you to create buttons using:
  * State managers
  * Triggers and actions


The difference between the two approaches is that when you use the state manager you always know in which state the button is. For example, when a user clicks a button created with triggers and actions, the action sends the message, but your application is not aware of the state of the button. When you use the state manager, you can always check which state the button is in and even revert the state when needed. See [Using state managers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/state-managers/using-state-managers.html).
When you use triggers and actions to create a button, and the user clicks the visual representation of a button, the action generates a message that travels to the button node where you can define the behavior for that message.
When you create a Button node, Kanzi Studio by default adds a Button: Click trigger to that node.
The Button nodes have the Focusable property enabled and can receive focus by default. When a Button node has focus, to press that button, you can use the default keyboard keys `Space`, `Enter`, and `Enter` on the numeric pad.
See [Using focus](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/focus/setting-focus.html).
You can add other triggers to a Button node as well. For example, you can add messages that are triggered when a user presses down a mouse button or cancels a click. See [Using triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html).
When you create a button it does not have a visual shape. To make a button visible, add to the button a node with content. You can make a Button 2D node visible also by filling its background with a brush. See [Adjusting the appearance of 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/adjusting-the-appearance.html).
![../../_images/button1.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/button1.gif)
The Kanzi Factory Content asset package contains a 2D button that you can customize. See [Button](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#fc-button).
To learn how to create a button, complete [Tutorial: Creating a button](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/button/button.html).
## Creating a button[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-buttons.html#creating-a-button "Link to this heading")
To create a button:
  1. In the Prefabs or Node Tree press `Alt` and right-click the node where you want to create a button and select either Button 3D, or Button 2D.
You can create a 3D node only in a 3D node, such as the Scene node, and a 2D node only in a 2D node.
![../../_images/create-button-2d1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-button-2d1.png)
  2. Define the content and appearance of the button.
For example, if you created a Button 2D node, add to it a Text Block 2D node that shows the button label, and in the Button 2D node set the Layout Width, Layout Height, and Background Brush properties. See [Adjusting the appearance of 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/adjusting-the-appearance.html).
![../../_images/select-button1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/select-button1.png) ![../../_images/button-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/button-in-preview.png)
Tip
Use a Content Layout node to create the layout for a button that contains multiple content nodes. See [Using the Content Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/using-content-layouts.html).
![../../_images/navigation-button-in-preview-5.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/navigation-button-in-preview-5.png)
  3. In the Prefabs or Node Tree select the Button node, in the Node Components > Triggers section in the Button: Click message trigger press `Alt` and right-click Actions, and select an action that you want to set off when the user presses the button.
For example, select the Write Log action and set its Log Text property to <Name>. In the Preview when you click the visual representation of the button, the Write Log action writes the name of that node to the Log window.
To learn more about the Write Log action, see [Using Write Log action](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/logging/write-log-action.html).
![../../_images/create-write-log-action.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-write-log-action.png) ![../../_images/set-write-log-text.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-write-log-text.png)
  4. (Optional) Use the Button triggers that come with Kanzi to define the behavior of Button nodes. See [Using triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html) and [Button node triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/reference-for-triggers.html#button-triggers).


## Controlling the behavior of a Button node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-buttons.html#controlling-the-behavior-of-a-button-node "Link to this heading")
In Kanzi, to control the behavior of a Button node you can:
  * Use a state manager to define how a Button node reacts to user input. See [Using a state manager to set button states](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-buttons.html#using-a-state-manager-to-set-button-states) and [Controlling whether a Button node is in use](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-buttons.html#button-enabled-disabled).
  * Use the Button triggers that come with Kanzi to define the behavior of Button nodes. See [Using the Button triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-buttons.html#using-button-triggers).
  * Enable users to double-click or double-tap Button nodes. See [Enabling the double-click gesture for a Button node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-buttons.html#enabling-double-click-gesture-for-button-node).


### Using a state manager to set button states[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-buttons.html#using-a-state-manager-to-set-button-states "Link to this heading")
Use a state manager to define how a Button node reacts to user input. For example, you can set how a button looks when the user presses or releases that button. You can see how to use state managers in [Using state managers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/state-managers/using-state-managers.html). To learn more about creating buttons using a state manager, see [Tutorial: Creating a button](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/button/button.html).
To use a state manager to set button states:
  1. In the Node Tree select the Button node for which you want to create states and in the State Tools create a state manager for that node.
![../../_images/select-button1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/select-button1.png) ![../../_images/create-state-manager-for-button.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-state-manager-for-button.png)
  2. Create two states, one that defines the button in its default state, and another that defines the button when it is pressed.
For example, name the states Default and Pressed.
![../../_images/create-two-states.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-two-states.png)
  3. For each state, set the values of the properties that set the appearance of the Button node.
For example, to set how a Button 2D node looks when the user presses it, for the Pressed state in that Button 2D node set:
     * Background Brush to the brush that you want to use when the button is pressed
     * Transform 2D > Render Transformation property Translation property fields to slightly larger values than in the default state
![../../_images/button-pressed-state-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/button-pressed-state-properties.png) ![../../_images/set-state-property-values.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-state-property-values.png)
  4. In the State Tools for the state manager which controls the Button states set the Controller Property to Is Down.
In a state manager, the value of the property that you select as the Controller Property defines the conditions when each state in a state group is active.
Here you use the Is Down property to transition to a state based on the value of that property.
The Is Down property controls whether a Button node is in a pressed or non-pressed state.
![../../_images/select-is-down-controller-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/select-is-down-controller-property.png)
  5. In the State Tools set the value of the Controller Property in the Pressed state to True.
This way you set your application to use the Pressed state when the button is pressed and the Default state when the button is not pressed.
![../../_images/set-is-down-values.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-is-down-values.png)
  6. In the State Tools, click Edit State Manager to deactivate the State Tools.
![../../_images/exit-state-tools1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/exit-state-tools1.png)
  7. (Optional) To set Kanzi to transition instantly between the button states, in the State Tools click the Any -> Any transition, in the State Transition Settings set the Duration property to 0, and click Save.
![../../_images/open-state-transition-settings.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/open-state-transition-settings.png) ![../../_images/state-transition-duration-0.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/state-transition-duration-0.png)


In the Preview when you click the button, the button enters the Pressed state and its appearance changes. The button stays in the Pressed state as long as you hold down the mouse button. When you release the mouse button, the button returns to the Default state.
![../../_images/button-press.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/button-press.gif)
### Controlling whether a Button node is in use[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-buttons.html#controlling-whether-a-button-node-is-in-use "Link to this heading")
To control whether a Button node is in use, use the Input > Enabled property. A disabled Button node does not produce user events, such as button presses.
When you disable the Enabled property of a node, you effectively disable that node and its descendant nodes in the same overlay focus scope.
To observe whether a node is effectively enabled, use the Input > Effectively Enabled property in a state manager or a binding. For example, to visually indicate to the user whether a node is in use, create a state manager and use the Effectively Enabled property as its controller property.
See [Controlling how a node reacts to input](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/handling-input.html#controlling-how-a-node-reacts-to-input).
### Using the Button triggers[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-buttons.html#using-the-button-triggers "Link to this heading")
Use the Button triggers that come with Kanzi to define the behavior of Button nodes. To learn more about using triggers, see [Using triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html).
  * Cancel trigger is set off:
    * When the user first presses down the button, then moves the pointer outside of the button area, and lifts the pointer.
    * When the user sets off a Long Press trigger.
  * Button: Click trigger is set off when the user presses down and then releases the button while the pointer is still within the button area.
  * Down trigger is set off when the user presses down the button.
  * Enter trigger is set off:
    * When the user presses down the button.
    * When the user presses down the button, moves the pointer outside of the button area, and then moves the pointer back to the button area while still holding down the pointer.
  * Leave trigger is set off:
    * When the user presses down the button and then lifts the pointer.
    * When the user presses down the button and then moves the pointer outside of the button area.
    * When the user sets off a Long Press trigger.
  * Long Press trigger is set off when the user presses down the button and holds the button pressed for the amount of milliseconds defined in the Hold Interval property of that button.


### Enabling the double-click gesture for a Button node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-buttons.html#enabling-the-double-click-gesture-for-a-button-node "Link to this heading")
Use the double-click gesture to enable users to double-click or double-tap buttons in your Kanzi application. Use the Multi-Click trigger to react to the double-click gesture. For example, you can change the appearance of a Button node when the user double-clicks or double-taps that node.
To enable the double-click gesture for a Button node:
  1. In the Node Tree or Prefabs select the Button node for which you want to enable the double-click gesture and in the Properties add and enable the Input > Double-Click Enabled property.
When you enable the Double-Click Enabled property, Kanzi installs in the Button node a multi-click manipulator that generates double-click messages.
![../../_images/select-button1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/select-button1.png) ![../../_images/double-click-enabled1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/double-click-enabled1.png)
  2. In the Node Components press `Alt` and right-click Triggers and select Message Trigger > Multi-Click > Multi-Click.
![../../_images/add-multi-click-trigger.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-multi-click-trigger.png)
  3. In the Node Components > Triggers press `Alt` and right-click the Multi-Click trigger, select an action, and configure the action. See [Using triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html) and [Actions and messages reference](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/reference-for-actions.html).


## Setting the appearance of a Button 2D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-buttons.html#setting-the-appearance-of-a-button-2d-node "Link to this heading")
To set the appearance of 2D nodes:
  * You can fill 2D nodes with a solid color, a texture, or a material. See [Adjusting the appearance of 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/adjusting-the-appearance.html).
![../../_images/color-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/color-brush.png) ![../../_images/texture-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/texture-brush.png) ![../../_images/material-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/material-brush.png)
  * You can apply a post-processing effect to a 2D node. See [Effects for 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/2d-effects.html).
![../../_images/blur-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blur-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/mask-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mask-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/outline-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/outline-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/shadow-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/shadow-effect-2d.png)
  * You can rotate a 2D node around all three axes to create a 3D perspective effect. See [Creating a 3D perspective effect for 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/setting-the-perspective.html).
![../../_images/perspective-transformation-visualization.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/perspective-transformation-visualization.png)
  * You can apply custom rendering to 2D nodes to create post-processing effects. See [Applying custom rendering to 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/applying-custom-rendering.html).
![../../_images/texture-grayscale.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/texture-grayscale.png)
  * You can render a 2D node as pixel-perfect. See [Rendering pixel-perfect 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/adjusting-the-appearance.html#rendering-pixel-perfect-2d-nodes).
![../../_images/snap-to-pixel-icon.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/snap-to-pixel-icon.png)


## Using the Button 3D node in the API[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-buttons.html#using-the-button-3d-node-in-the-api "Link to this heading")
For details, see the `Button3D[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a17866.html)` class.
## Using the Button 2D node in the API[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-buttons.html#using-the-button-2d-node-in-the-api "Link to this heading")
For details, see the `Button2D[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a17862.html)` class.
##  Button property types and messages[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-buttons.html#button-property-types-and-messages "Link to this heading")
For lists of the available property types and messages for the Button nodes, see [Button 2D](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/node-and-resource-reference/button-2d-reference.html) and [Button 3D](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/node-and-resource-reference/button-3d-reference.html).

# Using the Text Box nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#using-the-text-box-nodes "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Use the Text Box nodes to add single-line text input to your application.
Use Text Box 3D to add text input in 3D space and Text Box 2D to add text input in 2D space.
![../../_images/text-box.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box.gif)
The Text Box nodes have the Focusable property enabled and can receive focus by default. By default when a Text Box node has focus, that Text Box node is in the editing state.
When a Text Box node is in the editing state, to move the cursor in that text box, you can use these default keyboard keys:
  * `←` to move the cursor one character backward.
  * `→` to move the cursor one character forward.
  * `Ctrl` `←` to move the cursor to the word boundary that precedes the cursor.
  * `Ctrl` `→` to move the cursor to the word boundary that follows the cursor.
  * `Home` to move the cursor to the beginning of the text content.
  * `End` to move the cursor to the end of the text content.


When a Text Box node is in the editing state, to modify the text selection in that text box, you can use these default keyboard keys:
  * `Shift` `←` to move the active cursor in the text selection one character backward.
  * `Shift` `Ctrl` to move the active cursor in the text selection to the word boundary that precedes the current position.
  * `Shift` `Home` to move the active cursor in the text selection to the beginning of the text content.
  * `Shift` `→` to move the active cursor in the text selection one character forward.
  * `Shift` `Ctrl` `→` to move the active cursor in the text selection to the word boundary that follows the current position.
  * `Shift` `End` to move the active cursor in the text selection to the end of the text content.
  * `Ctrl` `A` to select all text.


Note
The TextBox2D is only implemented for Windows platforms, and to use it you need to include the following snippet to `registerMetadataOverride` in your application code:

```
#if defined WIN32
    WindowsImeBackend::registerModule(getDomain());
#endif

```
Copy to clipboard
## Editing the text in a Text Box node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#editing-the-text-in-a-text-box-node "Link to this heading")
A Text Box node by default:
  * Enters the editing state when focus moves to that Text Box node. This happens when the application user taps the node or sets focus to the node using the focus chain navigation. See [Focus](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/focus/focus.html).
  * Exits the editing state when focus moves from that Text Box node to another node.


See [Controlling manually when a Text Box node is in the editing state](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#controll).
To edit the text in a Text Box node:
  1. In the Node Tree press `Alt` and right-click the node where you want to add single-line text input to your application and select either Text Box 2D, or Text Box 3D.
You can create a 3D node only in a 3D node, such as the Scene node, and a 2D node only in a 2D node.
![../../_images/create-text-box-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-text-box-2d.png) ![../../_images/text-box-2d-in-node-tree.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-2d-in-node-tree.png)
  2. In the Node Tree create a node that you use to add, edit, and remove text in a Text Box node.
For example, create a Button 2D node and add content to it.
![../../_images/text-box-button-in-node-tree.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-button-in-node-tree.png)
  3. In the Node Tree select the node that you created in the previous step and in the Node Components > Triggers section press `Alt` and right-click the trigger that you want to use to add, edit, or remove text, and select one of the Text Box actions. See [Text Box actions](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/reference-for-actions.html#text-box-actions).
For example:
     * Insert Text At Cursor
Inserts text at the cursor position.
In the Insert Text At Cursor action set the value of the Text property to the text that you want to insert.
     * Delete At Cursor
Deletes a character using delete.
     * Backspace At Cursor
Deletes a character using backspace.
     * Move Cursor Backward
Moves the cursor one character backward.
     * Move Cursor Forward
Moves the cursor one character forward.
![../../_images/create-insert-text-at-cursor-action.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-insert-text-at-cursor-action.png) ![../../_images/insert-text-at-cursor.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/insert-text-at-cursor.png)
  4. In the action that you created in the previous step, set the Target Item to the Text Box node where you want to edit the text.
When the trigger, to which you added the action, is set off, Kanzi executes the action that edits the text in the Text Box node.
![../../_images/insert-text-at-cursor-target-item.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/insert-text-at-cursor-target-item.png)


## Controlling manually when a Text Box node is in the editing state[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#controlling-manually-when-a-text-box-node-is-in-the-editing-state "Link to this heading")
The application user can edit the text in a Text Box node when that node is in the editing state. Only one Text Box node can be in the editing state at a time. A Text Box node always leaves the editing state when:
  * Another Text Box node enters the editing state.
  * That Text Box node is disabled. See [Controlling whether a Text Box node is in use](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#text-box-enabled).


A Text Box node by default:
  * Enters the editing state when focus moves to that Text Box node. This happens when the application user taps the node or sets focus to the node using the focus chain navigation. See [Focus](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/focus/focus.html).
  * Exits the editing state when focus moves from that Text Box node to another node.


To manually control when a Text Box node is in the editing state:
  1. In the Node Tree select a Text Box node, in the Properties add the Edit Mode property, and set it to Triggered.
This way you set a Text Box node to:
     * Enter the editing state when a trigger executes the Text Box: Enter Editing State action.
     * Exit the editing state when either:
       * A trigger executes the Text Box: Leave Editing State action.
       * Another Text Box node enters the editing state.
![../../_images/text-box-2d-in-node-tree.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-2d-in-node-tree.png) ![../../_images/text-box-edit-mode.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-edit-mode.png)
  2. Create a trigger that sets the Text Box node to the editing state.
For example, to set the Text Box node to the editing state when the application user clicks a button, in the Node Tree create a Button node, in the Node Components in the Button: Click trigger create a Text Box: Enter Editing State action, and set Target Item to the Text Box node that you want to edit.
![../../_images/text-box-button-in-node-tree.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-button-in-node-tree.png) ![../../_images/enter-editing-state.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/enter-editing-state.png)
  3. Create a trigger that sets the Text Box node to exit the editing state.
For example, to set the Text Box node to exit the editing state when it loses focus, in that Text Box node create a Focus: Focus Lost trigger that executes a Text Box: Leave Editing State action.
![../../_images/text-box-2d-in-node-tree.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-2d-in-node-tree.png) ![../../_images/leave-editing-state.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/leave-editing-state.png)


## Limiting the length of text in a Text Box node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#limiting-the-length-of-text-in-a-text-box-node "Link to this heading")
In the Text Box nodes you can set:
  * The length of the text that the Text Box node can show. See [Setting the length of text that a Text Box node can show](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#setting-text-length-1).
  * The length of the text that the user can enter in the Text Box node. See [Setting the length of text that the user can enter in a Text Box node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#setting-text-length-2).


### Setting the length of text that a Text Box node can show[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#setting-the-length-of-text-that-a-text-box-node-can-show "Link to this heading")
To set the length of text that a Text Box node can show at a time, in the Node Tree select that node and in the Properties set the value of the Layout Width property.
![../../_images/text-box-2d-layout-width.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-2d-layout-width.png) ![../../_images/text-box-width-300.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-width-300.png)
When the text in a Text Box node is longer than the width of that node, in the editing state the user can scroll the text by moving the cursor in that Text Box node.
![../../_images/text-box-2d-scrolling.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-2d-scrolling.gif)
To let the length of the text in a Text Box node determine the width of that Text Box node, remove the Layout Width property.
### Setting the length of text that the user can enter in a Text Box node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#setting-the-length-of-text-that-the-user-can-enter-in-a-text-box-node "Link to this heading")
To set the length of text that the user can enter in a Text Box node, in the Node Tree select the Text Box node, in the Properties add the Maximum Text Length property, and set it to the number of UTF-8 characters to which you want to limit the text that the user can enter in that Text Box node.
![../../_images/text-box-maximum-text-length.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-maximum-text-length.png)
## Setting the color of text in a Text Box 2D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#setting-the-color-of-text-in-a-text-box-2d-node "Link to this heading")
To set the color of text in a Text Block 2D or Text Box 2D node:
  1. In the Node Tree create or select a Text Block 2D or Text Box 2D node.
![../../_images/select-text-block-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/select-text-block-2d.png)
  2. In the Properties add the Foreground Brush property.
![../../_images/add-foreground-brush-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-foreground-brush-property.png)
  3. Set the Foreground Brush property to an existing Color Brush or select + Color Brush, name the brush, click ![image0](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/quick-edit-properties.png) next to the property, and set the color of the Color Brush you created.
![../../_images/select-and-set-color-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/select-and-set-color-brush.png)
Tip
To quickly edit a brush, in the Properties next to the Background Brush or Foreground Brush property click ![quick-edit-property](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/quick-edit-properties.png) and edit the brush.
![../../_images/background-brush-quick-edit.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/background-brush-quick-edit.png)


## Setting the color of text in a Text Box 3D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#setting-the-color-of-text-in-a-text-box-3d-node "Link to this heading")
To set the color of text in a 3D text node:
  1. In the Node Tree create or select a Text Block 3D or Text Box 3D node.
![../../_images/create-text-block-3d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-text-block-3d.png)
  2. In the Properties add and set the Font Color property.
![../../_images/set-font-color.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-font-color.png)


## Setting the appearance of the cursor[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#setting-the-appearance-of-the-cursor "Link to this heading")
You can set the appearance of a Text Box cursor. To see the cursor of a Text Box node in the Kanzi Studio Preview click that Text Box node.
![../../_images/text-box-default-cursor.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-default-cursor.png)
To set the appearance of the cursor:
  1. In the Prefabs create a prefab that you want to use as the cursor.
For example, for a Text Box 2D node create an Empty Node 2D node and set its Background Brush, Layout Width, and Layout Height properties.
![../../_images/cursor-prefabs.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/cursor-prefabs.png) ![../../_images/cursor-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/cursor-properties.png) ![../../_images/cursor-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/cursor-preview.png)
  2. In the Node Tree select a Text Box node and in the Properties add and set the Cursor Prefab property to the prefab that you want to use as the cursor.
The Text Box node aligns the top of the cursor with the top of the Text Box node.
If the cursor does not fit in a Text Box 2D node, in the Text Box 2D node set the Horizontal Padding and Vertical Padding properties to adjust the offset of the cursor position.
![../../_images/text-box-cursor-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-cursor-properties.png) ![../../_images/text-box-cursor-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-cursor-preview.png)


## Setting the appearance of the text selection in a Text Box 2D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#setting-the-appearance-of-the-text-selection-in-a-text-box-2d-node "Link to this heading")
In a Text Box node you can set the color of the selected text, its background, and the handles to change the selected text.
To select a word in a Text Box node, double-click that word. To modify the selection, drag the handles in the top-left and bottom-right corners of the selected text.
![../../_images/text-box-selection-preview-default.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-selection-preview-default.png)
To set the appearance of text selection, in the Node Tree select a Text Box 2D node and in the Properties add and set:  
| Selection Background Brush to the brush that you want to use to fill the background of the selected text.  |  ![../../_images/selection-background-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/selection-background-brush.png)  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Selection Foreground Brush to the brush that you want to use to fill the selected text.  |  ![../../_images/selection-foreground-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/selection-foreground-brush.png)  |  
| Selection Start Prefab to the prefab that you want to use for the selection handle at the beginning of the selection.  |  ![../../_images/selection-start-prefab.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/selection-start-prefab.png)  |

## Setting the appearance of the composition text in a Text Box 2D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#setting-the-appearance-of-the-composition-text-in-a-text-box-2d-node "Link to this heading")
Composition text is an instance of text that the application user produces using an input method editor (IME). An input method editor is an application that enables the user to use their input devices to type characters and symbols that are not natively available on those input devices.
In a Text Box node you can set the color of the composition text and its background.
To set the appearance of the composition text, in the Node Tree select a Text Box 2D node and in the Properties add and set:
  * Composition Text Background Brush to the brush that you want to use to fill the background of the composition text.
  * Composition Text Foreground Brush to the brush that you want to use to fill the composition text.

![../../_images/text-box-2d-composition-appearance.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-2d-composition-appearance.png)
## Setting the appearance of the composition text in a Text Box 3D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#setting-the-appearance-of-the-composition-text-in-a-text-box-3d-node "Link to this heading")

To set the appearance of the composition text, in the Node Tree select a Text Box 3D node and in the Properties add and set:

## Showing placeholder content[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#showing-placeholder-content "Link to this heading")
You can set a Text Box node to show placeholder content when the Text Box is empty. For example, you can use this placeholder content to show text that tells the user what they can enter in a Text Box node.
To show placeholder content:
  1. In the Prefabs create a prefab that you want to use as the placeholder content.
For example, create a Text Block node and set its Text property.
![../../_images/hint-prefabs.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/hint-prefabs.png) ![../../_images/hint-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/hint-properties.png) ![../../_images/hint-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/hint-preview.png)
  2. In the Node Tree select a Text Box node and in the Properties add and set:
     * Text Hint Prefab to the prefab that you want to use as the placeholder content
     * (Optional) Hide Text Hint When Editing to enabled to hide the placeholder content whenever that Text Box node is in the editing state. By default Kanzi keeps the placeholder content visible until the user enters some text in the Text Box.
![../../_images/text-box-placeholder-text-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-placeholder-text-properties.png) ![../../_images/text-box-hint-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-hint-preview.png)


## Masking passwords[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#masking-passwords "Link to this heading")
You can set how to mask the password characters that the user enters in a Text Box node.
To set how Kanzi masks passwords in a Text Box node, in the Node Tree select that node, and in the Properties add and set:
  * Echo Mode to Password This way you set Kanzi to show each character for a certain amount of time, and then hide it with a masking character.
  * Password Echo Timeout to the time in milliseconds that you want to show each character before hiding it. By default Kanzi shows each character for one second.
  * Password Masking Character to the UTF-8 character with which you want to hide each password character. By default Kanzi masks each character with a bullet symbol (•).

![../../_images/text-box-password-mode-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-password-mode-properties.png) ![../../_images/password.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/password.gif)
## Setting truncation in a Text Box[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#setting-truncation-in-a-text-box "Link to this heading")
When a Text Box node is not in the editing state, if the text in the node is longer than the width of that node, Kanzi by default truncates the end part of the text with ellipsis. When a Text Box node is in the editing state, Kanzi does not truncate the text. Instead, the user can scroll the text by moving the cursor.
You can set:
  * Which part of the text to truncate. See [Setting the part to truncate](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#setting-the-part-to-truncate).
  * The type of truncation boundary. See [Setting the truncation boundary](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#setting-the-truncation-boundary).
  * How to indicate truncated text. See [Setting the characters that indicate truncation](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#setting-the-characters-that-indicate-truncation).


### Setting the part to truncate[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#setting-the-part-to-truncate "Link to this heading")
To set which part of the text to truncate, add the Text Concept > Truncation Direction property and set it to:
  * Trailing to truncate the end part of the text. Default value.
![../../_images/properties-truncation-mode-trailing.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-truncation-mode-trailing.png) [![../../_images/preview-truncation-mode-trailing.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-truncation-mode-trailing.png)](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-truncation-mode-trailing.png)
  * Center to truncate the middle part of the text.
![../../_images/properties-truncation-mode-middle.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-truncation-mode-middle.png) [![../../_images/preview-truncation-mode-middle.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-truncation-mode-middle.png)](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-truncation-mode-middle.png)
  * Leading to truncate the beginning part of the text.
![../../_images/properties-truncation-mode-leading.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-truncation-mode-leading.png) [![../../_images/preview-truncation-mode-leading.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-truncation-mode-leading.png)](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-truncation-mode-leading.png)


### Setting the truncation boundary[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#setting-the-truncation-boundary "Link to this heading")
To set the truncation boundary type, add the Text Concept > Truncation property and set it to:
  * None to disable text truncation. Kanzi clips the text at the node boundary.
![../../_images/properties-truncation-none.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-truncation-none.png) [![../../_images/preview-truncation-none.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-truncation-none.png)](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-truncation-none.png)
  * At character to truncate text character by character. Default value.
![../../_images/properties-truncation-at-character.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-truncation-at-character.png) [![../../_images/preview-truncation-mode-trailing.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-truncation-mode-trailing.png)](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-truncation-mode-trailing.png)
  * At word to truncate text by entire words.
![../../_images/properties-truncation-at-word.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-truncation-at-word.png) [![../../_images/preview-truncation-at-word.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-truncation-at-word.png)](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-truncation-at-word.png)


### Setting the characters that indicate truncation[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#setting-the-characters-that-indicate-truncation "Link to this heading")
To set the characters that indicate truncation, add and set the Overflow property.

## Using a binding to update the text in a Text Box node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#using-a-binding-to-update-the-text-in-a-text-box-node "Link to this heading")
To update the text in a Text Box node with a binding, use a to-source or two-way binding. See [Bindings](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/bindings.html).
For example, use a two-way binding to enable the user to edit a numerical value either by entering text in the Text Box node or by using a slider.
To use a binding to update the text in a Text Box node:
  1. In the Node Tree or Prefabs, create a Text Box node and set its appearance.
![../../_images/node-tree-text-box-in-stack-layout.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tree-text-box-in-stack-layout.png)
  2. Create a slider and set its lowest and highest value.
The Kanzi Factory Content contains a 2D slider that you can use. See [Using the slider from the Factory Content](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/sliders/using-sliders.html#using-slider-from-fc).
![../../_images/asset-packages-fc-slider.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/asset-packages-fc-slider.png) ![../../_images/node-tree-slider.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tree-slider.png) ![../../_images/slider-range-properties1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/slider-range-properties1.png)
  3. Select the Text Box node that you created. In the Properties, click + Add Binding and in the Binding Editor, set:
     * Binding Mode to Two way
     * Property to Text Concept > Text
     * Expression to point to the Value property of the slider that you created:

```
{@../Slider/RangeConcept.Value}

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/binding-editor-two-way-text-slider-value.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/binding-editor-two-way-text-slider-value.png)
  4. (Optional) Create another binding and in the Binding Editor, set:
     * Property to Text
     * Expression to

```
int(getCurrentValue())

```
Copy to clipboard
This binding gets the current value of the Text property and converts it to an integer.
![../../_images/binding-editor-text-modifier-binding.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/binding-editor-text-modifier-binding.png)


Now, in the Preview:
  * When you move the slider knob, the text changes.
  * When you edit the text, the slider knob moves.

![../../_images/preview-text-slider-control.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-text-slider-control.gif)
## Controlling whether a Text Box node is in use[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#controlling-whether-a-text-box-node-is-in-use "Link to this heading")
To control whether a Text Box node is in use, use the Input > Enabled property. A disabled Text Box node does not react to user input. When you disable a Text Box node, that Text Box node leaves the editing state and stays in that state while it is disabled.
When you disable the Enabled property of a node, you effectively disable that node and its descendant nodes in the same overlay focus scope.
To observe whether a node is effectively enabled, use the Input > Effectively Enabled property in a state manager or a binding. For example, to visually indicate to the user whether a node is in use, create a state manager and use the Effectively Enabled property as its controller property.
See [Controlling how a node reacts to input](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/handling-input.html#controlling-how-a-node-reacts-to-input).

## Using the Text Box 3D node in the API[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#using-the-text-box-3d-node-in-the-api "Link to this heading")
To create a Text Box 3D node:

```
// Create a Text Box 3D node named Text Box.
TextBox3DSharedPtr textBoxNode = TextBox3D::create(this->getDomain(), "Text Box");

```
Copy to clipboard
To set the initial text content in a Text Box 3D node:

```
// Set the initial text content in the Text Box node.
textBoxNode->setText("Initial text that the Text Box contains before editing.");

```
Copy to clipboard
To set the appearance of the text in a Text Box 3D node:

```
// Set the style of the text in the Text Box node:
// Set the font family of the text.
textBoxNode->setFontFamily(fontFamily);
// Set line spacing to 1.5f.
textBoxNode->setLineSpacing(1.5f);
// Set font size to 36.0f.
textBoxNode->setFontSize(36.0f);
// Set the color of the text to blue.
textBoxNode->setFontColor(ThemeBlue);
// Align the text to the right.
textBoxNode->setTextHorizontalAlignment(TextFormat::TextHorizontalAlignmentRight);
// Set font hinting: Render the text in the Text Box node using the hinter of the font engine rasterizer.
textBoxNode->setHintingPreference(FontHintingPreference::AutoHinting);

```
Copy to clipboard
To show placeholder content in a Text Box 3D node:

```
// Set the prefab that shows the placeholder content in the Text Box node.
textBoxNode->setTextHintPrefab(textHintPrefab);

```
Copy to clipboard
To set the position of the cursor in a Text Box 3D node:

```
// Set the cursor position in the beginning of the text field.
textBoxNode->setCursorPosition(0u);

```
Copy to clipboard
To set the appearance of the cursor in a Text Box 3D node:

```
// Set the prefab that visualizes the cursor.
textBoxNode->setCursorPrefab(cursorPrefab);

```
Copy to clipboard
To set the appearance of the text selection in a Text Box 3D node:

```
// Set the color of the selected text to orange.
textBoxNode->setSelectionFontColor(ThemeOrange);
// Set the background color of the selected text to gray.
textBoxNode->setSelectionBackgroundColor(ThemeGray);
// Set the prefab that visualizes the selection handle at the beginning of the selection.
textBoxNode->setCursorPrefab(selectionStartPrefab);
// Set the prefab that visualizes the selection handle at the end of the selection.
textBoxNode->setCursorPrefab(selectionEndPrefab);

```
Copy to clipboard
To set the appearance of the composition text in a Text Box 3D node:

```
// Set the color of the composition text to red.
textBoxNode->setSelectionFontColor(ThemeRed);
// Set the background color of the composition text to gray.
textBoxNode->setSelectionBackgroundColor(ThemeGray);

```
Copy to clipboard
To make a Text Box 3D node behave as a password field:

```
// Set Kanzi to show each character for a certain amount of time, and then hide it with a masking character.
textBoxNode->setEchoMode(EchoMode::Password);
// Set the UTF-8 character with which you want to hide each password character.
textBoxNode->setPasswordMaskingCharacter("*");
// Set the time in milliseconds that you want to show each character before hiding it.
textBoxNode->setPasswordEchoTimeout(500);

```
Copy to clipboard
For details, see the `TextBox3D[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a18870.html)` class.

# Using the Toggle Button nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-toggle-buttons.html#using-the-toggle-button-nodes "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Use the Toggle Button nodes to create interactions through buttons that can have multiple toggle states.
See [Creating a toggle button with two states](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-toggle-buttons.html#creating-a-toggle-button-with-two-states) and [Creating a toggle button with more than two states](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-toggle-buttons.html#creating-a-toggle-button-with-more-than-two-states).
Use the Toggle Button 3D to create a 3D toggle button and the Toggle Button 2D to create a 2D toggle button. After you create a Toggle Button node, add to it nodes to create a visual representation of the toggle button.
![../../_images/toggle-button1.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/toggle-button1.gif)
When you create a Toggle Button, Kanzi by default adds to that node the Toggle Button: triggers:
  * Toggle Button: Toggled On
  * Toggle Button: Toggled Off
  * Toggle Button: State Toggled


See [Reacting to toggle changes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-toggle-buttons.html#using-toggle-button-triggers).
The Toggle Button nodes have the Focusable property enabled and can receive focus by default. When a Toggle Button node has focus, to press that button, you can use the default keyboard keys `Space`, `Enter`, and `Enter` on the numeric pad.
See [Using focus](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/focus/setting-focus.html).
For example, to show the difference between the on and off states of a toggle button, you can:
  * Switch the material or color of the visual representation of the toggle button.
  * Attach two different visual representations of the toggle button and switch their visibility.
  * Attach two different visual representations of the toggle button and transition between the two by animating their Blend Intensity property value.


To learn how to create a toggle button, complete the toggle button tutorial. See [Tutorial: Creating a toggle button](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/toggle-button/toggle-button.html).
## Creating a toggle button with two states[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-toggle-buttons.html#creating-a-toggle-button-with-two-states "Link to this heading")
To create a toggle button with two states:
  1. In the Node Tree press `Alt` and right-click the node where you want to create a toggle button and select either Toggle Button 3D, or Toggle Button 2D.
You can create a 3D node only in a 3D node, such as the Scene node, and a 2D node only in a 2D node.
![../../_images/create-toggle-button-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-toggle-button-2d.png)
  2. In the Node Tree select the Toggle Button node and in the State Tools click Create State Manager to create a state manager in the Toggle Button node.
![../../_images/create-state-manager2.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-state-manager2.png)
  3. In the State Tools, click Create State twice to create two states. Double-click the name of each state and rename the states.
For example, name one state On and the other Off.
The On state defines the state of your application when the toggle button is toggled on, the Off state when the toggle button is toggled off.
![../../_images/rename-toggle-button-states.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/rename-toggle-button-states.png)
  4. In the Node Tree create a visual shape for the Toggle Button node, and set its appearance for when it is in the On state.
For example, if you created a Toggle Button 2D node, add to that node an Image node which represents the indicator that shows when the toggle button is toggled on and off.
![../../_images/create-indicator.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-indicator.png)
  5. Position the indicator in the Preview and in the State Tools click ![image0](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/store-current-values.png) above the On state to save the current appearance to that state.
![../../_images/add-indicator-to-on-state.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-indicator-to-on-state.png)
  6. Repeat the previous two steps to create the Off state for the toggle button.
![../../_images/add-indicator-to-off-state.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-indicator-to-off-state.png)
  7. In the State Tools, click the <No Controller Property> dropdown menu and select the Toggle Button > Toggle State property.
In a state manager, the value of the property that you select as the Controller Property defines the conditions when each state in a state group is active.
![../../_images/toggle-state-controller-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/toggle-state-controller-property.png)
  8. In the State Tools, set the value of the controller property for each state.
     * For the On state set the value to 1.
     * For the Off state leave the value set to 0.
![../../_images/set-controller-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-controller-property.png)
  9. In the State Tools, click Edit State Manager to deactivate the State Tools.
![../../_images/deactivate-state-tools.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/deactivate-state-tools.png)
  10. In the Preview when you click the visual representation of the toggle button, you toggle between the states you created, and the appearance of the toggle button changes.


## Creating a toggle button with more than two states[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-toggle-buttons.html#creating-a-toggle-button-with-more-than-two-states "Link to this heading")
To create a toggle button with more than two states:
  1. In the Node Tree press `Alt` and right-click the node where you want to create a toggle button and select either Toggle Button 3D, or Toggle Button 2D.
You can create a 3D node only in a 3D node, such as the Scene node, and a 2D node only in a 2D node.
  2. In the Node Tree select the Toggle Button node and in the Properties add and set the Toggle State Count property to as many toggle states you want the toggle button to have.
For example, to create a toggle button with three states, set the Toggle State Count property to 3.
![../../_images/toggle-state-count-set-3.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/toggle-state-count-set-3.png)
  3. In the Node Tree select the Toggle Button node and in the State Tools click Create State Manager to create a state manager in the Toggle Button node.
  4. In the State Tools click ![image1](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-page-button.png) as many times as you want to create states, double-click the name of each state, and rename the states.
For example, if you are creating a toggle button with three states name the first state First, the second state Second, and the third state Third. Each state defines the state of your application when the toggle button is in that state.
![../../_images/toggle-button-three-states.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/toggle-button-three-states.png)
  5. In the Node Tree create a visual shape for the Toggle Button node, and set its appearance for when it is in the first state.
For example, if you created a 3D toggle button, add a Text Block 3D and set the Text property to First.
  6. In the State Tools click ![image3](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/store-current-values.png) above the First state to save the current appearance to that state.
![../../_images/toggle-button-save-first-state.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/toggle-button-save-first-state.png)
  7. Repeat the previous two steps as many times as you have states in the toggle button. For every state set a different value for the Text property and save the value to a different state.
  8. In the State Tools, click the <No Controller Property> dropdown menu and select the Toggle Button > Toggle State property.
In a state manager, the value of the property that you select as the Controller Property defines the conditions when each state in a state group is active.
![../../_images/toggle-state-controller-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/toggle-state-controller-property.png)
  9. In the State Tools set the value of the controller property for each state.
For example, for a toggle button with three states, set the value for the First state to 0, for the Second state to 1, and for the Third state to 2.
![../../_images/toggle-button-set-toggle-state-controller-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/toggle-button-set-toggle-state-controller-property.png)
  10. In the State Tools, click Edit State Manager to deactivate the State Tools.
  11. In the Preview when you click the visual representation of the toggle button, you toggle between the states you created, and the appearance of the toggle button changes.


## Reacting to toggle changes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-toggle-buttons.html#reacting-to-toggle-changes "Link to this heading")
You can use the Toggle Button triggers to react when the user toggles a toggle button. To learn more about using triggers, see [Using triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html).
When you create a Toggle Button node, Kanzi by default adds these triggers to that node:  
| Name  | Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
| State Toggled  | State Toggled trigger is set off when the toggle state of a Toggle Button node changes.  |  
| Toggled Off  | Toggled Off trigger is set off when a Toggle Button node with two states is toggled off.  |  
| Toggled On  | Toggled On trigger is set off when a Toggle Button node with two states is toggled on.  |  
To react to toggle changes:
  1. In the Prefabs or Node Tree select the Toggle Button node to whose toggling you want to react.
For example, create a toggle button with two states and select that toggle button. See [Creating a toggle button with two states](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-toggle-buttons.html#creating-a-toggle-button-with-two-states).
  2. In the Node Components > Triggers press `Alt` and right-click a Toggle Button trigger, select the action that you want to set off, and configure that action.
For example, in the Toggle Button: Toggled On trigger create a Write Log action and set Log Text to the message that you want to write to the Log window when the user toggles on the toggle button.
To learn more about the Write Log action, see [Using Write Log action](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/logging/write-log-action.html).
![../../_images/toggled-on-add-write-log.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/toggled-on-add-write-log.png) ![../../_images/write-log-toggled-on.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/write-log-toggled-on.png)


## Using a binding to update the toggle state[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-toggle-buttons.html#using-a-binding-to-update-the-toggle-state "Link to this heading")
To update the toggle state of a Toggle Button node with a binding, use a to-source or two-way binding. When you toggle a Toggle Button, that Toggle Button internally overrides any one-way binding that targets the Toggle State property. See [Bindings](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/bindings.html).
For example, to use a to-source binding to update the toggle state:
  1. Create a Toggle Button node whose toggle state you want to update with a binding.
For example:
    1. In the Node Tree, create a Stack Layout 2D node.
![../../_images/stack-layout.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/stack-layout.png)
    2. From the Asset Packages > Factory Content, drag the Toggle Button to the Node Tree and drop it on the Stack Layout 2D node. See [Factory Content assets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html).
![../../_images/asset-packages-toggle-button.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/asset-packages-toggle-button.png) ![../../_images/node-tree-fc-toggle-button.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tree-fc-toggle-button.png)
  2. Create a control to which you want to bind the toggle state of the Toggle Button node.
For example:
    1. From the Asset Packages > Factory Content, drag the Slider to the Node Tree and drop it on the Stack Layout 2D node. In the Properties, add and set the lowest and highest value of the slider. See [Using the slider from the Factory Content](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/sliders/using-sliders.html#using-slider-from-fc).
![../../_images/asset-packages-fc-slider.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/asset-packages-fc-slider.png) ![../../_images/node-tree-fc-slider.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tree-fc-slider.png) ![../../_images/properties-slider-range1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-slider-range1.png)
    2. (Optional) In the Stack Layout 2D node, create a Text Block 2D node that shows the slider value.
![../../_images/node-tree-text-block-slider-value.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tree-text-block-slider-value.png) ![../../_images/properties-slider-value-binding.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-slider-value-binding.png) ![../../_images/preview-adjust-slider-value.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-adjust-slider-value.gif)
  3. Select the Toggle Button node. In the Properties, click + Add Binding and in the Binding Editor, set:
     * Binding Mode to To source
     * Push Target to .
     * Property to Toggle Button > Toggle State
     * Expression to the expression that returns the value to which you want to set the toggle state.
For example, set it to

```
{@../Slider/RangeConcept.Value} == 0 ? 0 : 1

```
Copy to clipboard
This binding uses the conditional operator to toggle the Toggle Button:
       * Off when the value of the Slider is zero.
       * On when the value of the Slider is not zero.
See [? (conditional)](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/reference-for-bindings-expressions.html#conditional).
Tip
You can start creating a binding for a property by right-clicking a property and selecting Create Binding.
This way you automatically add the property to the Binding Editor.
![../../_images/properties-create-binding.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-create-binding.png)
![../../_images/node-tree-fc-toggle-button-2.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tree-fc-toggle-button-2.png) ![../../_images/binding-editor-to-source-toggle-state.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/binding-editor-to-source-toggle-state.png)


Now, when in the Preview you:
  * Adjust the slider to a value larger than zero, Kanzi toggles on the toggle button.
  * Adjust the slider to zero, Kanzi toggles off the toggle button.
  * Toggle the toggle button, the slider keeps its value.


This enables the user to both adjust the value of a setting and quickly enable and disable the setting. For example, you can create a volume control.
![../../_images/preview-toggle-state-slider-control.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-toggle-state-slider-control.gif)
## Controlling whether a Toggle Button node is in use[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-toggle-buttons.html#controlling-whether-a-toggle-button-node-is-in-use "Link to this heading")
To control whether a Toggle Button node is in use, use the Input > Enabled property. A disabled Toggle Button node does not produce user events, such as button presses. When you disable a Toggle Button node, Kanzi preserves the toggled state of that Toggle Button node.
When you disable the Enabled property of a node, you effectively disable that node and its descendant nodes in the same overlay focus scope.
To observe whether a node is effectively enabled, use the Input > Effectively Enabled property in a state manager or a binding. For example, to visually indicate to the user whether a node is in use, create a state manager and use the Effectively Enabled property as its controller property.
See [Controlling how a node reacts to input](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/handling-input.html#controlling-how-a-node-reacts-to-input).
## Enabling the double-click gesture for a Toggle Button node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-toggle-buttons.html#enabling-the-double-click-gesture-for-a-toggle-button-node "Link to this heading")
Use the double-click gesture to enable users to double-click or double-tap toggle buttons in your Kanzi application. Use the Multi-Click trigger to react to the double-click gesture. For example, you can change the appearance of a Toggle Button node when the user double-clicks or double-taps that node.
To enable the double-click gesture for a Toggle Button node:
  1. In the Node Tree or Prefabs select the Toggle Button node for which you want to enable the double-click gesture and in the Properties add and enable the Input > Double-Click Enabled property.
When you enable the Double-Click Enabled property, Kanzi installs in the Toggle Button node a multi-click manipulator that generates double-click messages.
![../../_images/toggle-button-2d-in-prefabs.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/toggle-button-2d-in-prefabs.png) ![../../_images/toggle-button-double-click-enabled.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/toggle-button-double-click-enabled.png)
  2. In the Node Components press `Alt` and right-click Triggers and select Message Trigger > Multi-Click > Multi-Click.
![../../_images/add-multi-click-trigger.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-multi-click-trigger.png)
  3. In the Node Components > Triggers press `Alt` and right-click the Multi-Click trigger, select an action, and configure the action. See [Using triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html) and [Actions and messages reference](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/reference-for-actions.html).


## Setting the appearance of a Toggle Button 2D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-toggle-buttons.html#setting-the-appearance-of-a-toggle-button-2d-node "Link to this heading")
To set the appearance of 2D nodes:
  * You can fill 2D nodes with a solid color, a texture, or a material. See [Adjusting the appearance of 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/adjusting-the-appearance.html).
![../../_images/color-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/color-brush.png) ![../../_images/texture-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/texture-brush.png) ![../../_images/material-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/material-brush.png)
  * You can apply a post-processing effect to a 2D node. See [Effects for 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/2d-effects.html).
![../../_images/blur-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blur-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/mask-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mask-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/outline-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/outline-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/shadow-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/shadow-effect-2d.png)
  * You can rotate a 2D node around all three axes to create a 3D perspective effect. See [Creating a 3D perspective effect for 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/setting-the-perspective.html).
![../../_images/perspective-transformation-visualization.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/perspective-transformation-visualization.png)
  * You can apply custom rendering to 2D nodes to create post-processing effects. See [Applying custom rendering to 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/applying-custom-rendering.html).
![../../_images/texture-grayscale.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/texture-grayscale.png)
  * You can render a 2D node as pixel-perfect. See [Rendering pixel-perfect 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/adjusting-the-appearance.html#rendering-pixel-perfect-2d-nodes).
![../../_images/snap-to-pixel-icon.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/snap-to-pixel-icon.png)


## Using the Toggle Button 3D node in the API[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-toggle-buttons.html#using-the-toggle-button-3d-node-in-the-api "Link to this heading")
For details, see the `ToggleButton3D[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a18878.html)` class.
## Using the Toggle Button 2D node in the API[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-toggle-buttons.html#using-the-toggle-button-2d-node-in-the-api "Link to this heading")
For details, see the `ToggleButton2D[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a18874.html)` class.
##  Toggle Button property types and messages[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-toggle-buttons.html#toggle-button-property-types-and-messages "Link to this heading")
For lists of the available property types and messages for the Toggle Button nodes, see [Toggle Button 2D](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/node-and-resource-reference/toggle-button-2d-reference.html) and [Toggle Button 3D](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/node-and-resource-reference/toggle-button-3d-reference.html).
## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-toggle-buttons.html#sa "Link to this heading")

# Using the Grid List Box nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-list-boxes.html#using-the-grid-list-box-nodes "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
