Use the Grid List Box nodes to create scrollable lists of items arranged in a grid.
![../../_images/grid-list-box.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/grid-list-box.gif)
Learn how to use the Grid List Box nodes by completing a tutorial. See [Tutorial: Create a contacts list with a Grid List Box](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/list-box/list-box.html).
As you add items to a Grid List Box node, the Grid List Box node places them either in its first row or column:
  * When the items in the Grid List Box node reach the set width or height of the Grid List Box node, the Grid List Box node places the items in the next row or column.
  * When there are more items than fit in the width and height you set for a grid list box, the items become visible as you scroll the Grid List Box node.


To select an item in a Grid List Box node click that item.
The Grid List Box node arranges its items based on what you set in the Layout Direction property:
  * Right to arrange the items along the x axis.
When adding items, the Grid List Box node places each new item to the right of the item preceding it. When an item reaches or exceeds the width of the Grid List Box node, the Grid List Box node places that item into a new row.
Users can scroll the Grid List Box node on the y axis.
![../../_images/grid-list-box-right.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/grid-list-box-right.gif)
  * Down to arrange the items along the y axis.
When adding items, the Grid List Box node places each new item below the item preceding it. When an item reaches or exceeds the height of the Grid List Box node, the Grid List Box node places that item into a new column.
Users can scroll the Grid List Box node on the x axis.
![../../_images/grid-list-box-down.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/grid-list-box-down.gif)


You can use the Grid List Box > Reversed Scrolling property to reverse the direction of scrolling.
The Grid List Box nodes that you create in Kanzi Studio are focus scopes and handle the key focus and key input by default. See [Handling the key focus in a List Box node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/container-controls/list-box-nodes.html#lb-handling-key-focus).
Note
Items in all list box nodes (Grid List Box nodes and Trajectory List Box 3D node) are not its child nodes, even though in Kanzi Studio it seems so when you add items to a list box. Because list box items are not child nodes of a list box, you cannot refer to these items from outside of a list box using paths or aliases. If you need to refer from a list box item to an object outside of a list box, use bindings and aliases. See [Binding to properties outside of a Grid List Box node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-list-boxes.html#binding) and [Navigating to Page nodes from a Trajectory List Box 3D node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html#navigating).
## Creating a Grid List Box node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-list-boxes.html#creating-a-grid-list-box-node "Link to this heading")
To create a Grid List Box node:
  1. In the Node Tree press `Alt` and right-click the node where you want to create a Grid List Box node and select either Grid List Box 3D, or Grid List Box 2D.
You can create a 3D node only in a 3D node, such as the Scene node, and a 2D node only in a 2D node.
![../../_images/create-grid-list-box-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-grid-list-box-2d.png)
  2. In the Node Tree add items to the Grid List Box node.
Use a data source to add items to a List Box node. See [Using a data source](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/data-sources/using-a-data-source.html).
For example, to create a contact list, add several nodes which represent the contacts in the list. See [Using the List Box Item Container prefabs](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/container-controls/using-list-box-item-containers.html).
As you add items, the Grid List Box node arranges them in a grid from the top-left towards the bottom-right corner of the Grid List Box node. See [Setting how a Grid List Box node arranges its items](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-list-boxes.html#setting-how-glb-node-arranges-its-items).
To browse the items in a Grid List Box node, in the Preview click and drag the items in the Grid List Box node.
![../../_images/add-contact-items.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-contact-items.png) ![../../_images/contact-items-added.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/contact-items-added.png) ![../../_images/contact-items-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/contact-items-in-preview.png)
  3. (Optional) If you cannot see the content you added to a Grid List Box node or the content does not fully fit, add and set the Cell Height and Cell Width properties.
You set the area reserved for each element inside the list box. The cell size clips the items if the items do not fit in the cell.
![../../_images/cell-width-set.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/cell-width-set.png)
  4. In the Node Tree select the Grid List Box node and in the Properties set the Layout Height and Layout Width properties.
You set the area in which the items in the Grid List Box node are visible. If all items in the Grid List Box node do not fit in the area, Kanzi clips those items which do not fit. The user can scroll the Grid List Box node to access all items.
![../../_images/set-layout-height-width.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-layout-height-width.png)
  5. (Optional) In the Preview click ![image0](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/analyze-off.png) to enter the Analyze mode, right-click ![image1](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/analyze-on.png), and select Debug objects.
This way you visualize the borders of the Grid List Box node and the items in the Grid List Box node.
![../../_images/debug-objects-grid-list-box.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/debug-objects-grid-list-box.png)


## Setting how a Grid List Box node arranges its items[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-list-boxes.html#setting-how-a-grid-list-box-node-arranges-its-items "Link to this heading")
You can set the Grid List Box node so that it arranges its items either along the x or y axis.
To set how a Grid List Box arranges its items:
  1. Create a Grid List Box node and add items to it. See [Creating a Grid List Box node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-list-boxes.html#creating-glb).
  2. In the Properties set the Layout Direction property to either:
     * Right to arrange the items along the x axis.
When adding items, the Grid List Box node places each new item to the right of the item preceding it. When an item reaches or exceeds the width of the Grid List Box node, the Grid List Box node places that item into a new row.
Use the Layout Width and Layout Height properties to set the size of the Grid List Box node area.
Users can scroll the Grid List Box node on the y axis.
![../../_images/layout-direction-right.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/layout-direction-right.png) ![../../_images/layout-direction-right-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/layout-direction-right-in-preview.png)
     * Down to arrange the items along the y axis.
When adding items, the Grid List Box node places each new item below the item preceding it. When an item reaches or exceeds the height of the Grid List Box node, the Grid List Box node places that item into a new column. Use the Layout Width and Layout Height properties to set the size of the Grid List Box node area.
Users can scroll the Grid List Box node on the x axis.
![../../_images/layout-direction-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/layout-direction-property.png) ![../../_images/layout-direction-down-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/layout-direction-down-in-preview.png)


## Bringing the selected item to the center of a Grid List Box[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-list-boxes.html#bringing-the-selected-item-to-the-center-of-a-grid-list-box "Link to this heading")
You can set a Grid List Box node to bring the item to the center of the list box area when a user clicks that item.
To set items in a Grid List Box node to the center when the user selects them:
  1. Create a Grid List Box node and add items to it. See [Creating a Grid List Box node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-list-boxes.html#creating-glb).
  2. In the Properties add the Selection Behavior property and set it to Bring Center.
You set the Grid List Box node to scroll an item to the center of the node area when the user selects that item. The Grid List Box node centers its items based on the value you set in the Layout Direction property. See [Setting how a Grid List Box node arranges its items](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-list-boxes.html#setting-how-glb-node-arranges-its-items).
![../../_images/selection-behavior.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/selection-behavior.png) ![../../_images/bring-center-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/bring-center-in-preview.png)
  3. In the Properties add and set:
     * Item Area Begin to the offset where you want the area for the items in the Grid List Box node to begin.
For example, set it to 0.4.
     * Item Area End to the offset where you want the area for the items in the Grid List Box node to end.
For example, set it to 0.6.
Use the Item Area Begin and Item Area End properties to:
     * Grid List Box 2D. Set the items at the beginning and end of the list to also align to the center of the list when the user selects one of those items. For example, if the Grid List Box node has five items visible at a time, each of those items takes up 0.2 of the total area of the Grid List Box node. The centermost item takes up 0.1 of the space above it and 0.1 of the space below it.
     * Grid List Box 3D. Set the value of the Visible Amount In Parent property. Use the Visible Amount In Parent property to set shaders to change the appearance of an item based on the location of that object in the list box. For example, if you use the Visible Amount In Parent property to gradually change the visibility of an item, set the Item Area Begin property to a larger value and the Item Area End property to a smaller value. This way you limit the area where that item is visible.
![../../_images/item-area-begin-end.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/item-area-begin-end.png) ![../../_images/last-item-centered.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/last-item-centered.png)


## Nesting Grid List Box nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-list-boxes.html#nesting-grid-list-box-nodes "Link to this heading")
You can nest Grid List Box nodes to create a Grid List Box node within a Grid List Box node, each of which you can scroll independently. For example, you can create:
  * A list of albums with a vertically scrollable Grid List Box node of album categories which contains a nested Grid List Box node which you can scroll horizontally to browse each category.
  * A list of contacts with a vertically scrollable Grid List Box node of contacts which contains a nested Grid List Box node which you can scroll horizontally to edit or delete a contact.


In a Grid List Box node use the Layout Direction property to set how Grid List Box node arranges its items and to set the axis on which users can scroll. Set the Layout Direction to:
  * Right to scroll the list items on the y axis.
  * Down to scroll the list items on the x axis.


To nest Grid List Box nodes:
  1. Create a Grid List Box node. See [Creating a Grid List Box node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-list-boxes.html#creating-glb).
By default the value of the Layout Direction property is Right and you can scroll the list items on the y axis. To scroll the list items on the x axis, set the Layout Direction property to Down.
![../../_images/create-grid-list-box-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-grid-list-box-2d.png) ![../../_images/set-layout-direction.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-layout-direction.png)
  2. Create the structure for each list item of the Grid List Box node you created in the previous step.
For example, if you want to create several nested Grid List Box nodes which contain albums, in the Prefabs create a Stack Layout 2D node, and inside it create a Text Block 2D node.
You use the Stack Layout 2D node to position each nested Grid List Box and the album category title, and the Text Block 2D node to show the category title. See [Using the Stack Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/using-stack-layouts.html).
![../../_images/stack-layout-prefab.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/stack-layout-prefab.png)
  3. Create a Grid List Box node that you want to nest in the Grid List Box that you created in the first step, and set it to scroll on a different axis than its parent Grid List Box node. If you set the Layout Direction property to Right for the parent Grid List Box node, for the nested Grid List Box node set that property to Down to scroll that Grid List Box on the x axis.
For example, if you created a Stack Layout 2D prefab in the previous step, in that Stack Layout 2D create a Grid List Box node, and drag to the Node Tree to the Grid List Box node several instances of that prefab.
![../../_images/grid-list-box-prefab.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/grid-list-box-prefab.png) ![../../_images/layout-direction-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/layout-direction-property.png) ![../../_images/nested-list-boxes-in-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/nested-list-boxes-in-project.png)
  4. Add items to each nested Grid List Box node.
For example, to create a vertically scrollable Grid List Box which contains horizontally scrollable Grid List Box of albums, in the Prefabs create an Image node you use to represent each album, and drag to each nested Grid List Box several instances of that prefab.
You can add items to a Grid List Box using a data source. See [Using a data source](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/data-sources/using-a-data-source.html).
![../../_images/image-prefab.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/image-prefab.png) ![../../_images/images-in-list-boxes.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/images-in-list-boxes.png)


## Binding to properties outside of a Grid List Box node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-list-boxes.html#binding-to-properties-outside-of-a-grid-list-box-node "Link to this heading")
Use an alias when you want to bind a property of a list box item to a property of a node outside of the list box.
For example, if you have a Grid List Box 3D or a Trajectory List Box 3D node with a Text Block 3D node item and want to set the Text property value of the Text Block 3D node to a value of an Empty Node 3D node property that is not in the list box:
![../../_images/binding-outside-a-list-box---structure.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/binding-outside-a-list-box---structure.png)
  1. In the Node Tree press `Alt` and right-click the nodes that contain the property to which you want to bind and select Alias. See [Using aliases](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/aliases/using-aliases.html).
For example, create an alias for the Empty Node 3D node.
  2. In the Dictionaries make sure that the aliases you created are in the resource dictionary that the list box node can access.
For example, place all aliases to the resource dictionary of the Screen node, or create a resource dictionary in the list box node and place the aliases to that resource dictionary. See [Using resource dictionaries](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/resources/using-resource-dictionaries.html).
  3. Create the binding:
    1. In the Node Tree select the node inside the list box node from which you want to bind to a node outside of the list box node.
    2. In the Properties click + Add Binding and create the binding using the alias to bind to the property in a node outside of the list box node.
For example, in the Text Block 3D node create a binding to the Empty Node 3D node using the alias you created in the first step. See [Bindings expressions reference](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/reference-for-bindings-expressions.html).
For example, use this binding expression:

```
{#Empty Node 3D/TextConcept.Text}

```
Copy to clipboard
The Text property in the Text Block 3D node gets the value of the Text property from the Empty Node 3D node.
    3. Click Save.


## Navigating to Page nodes from a Grid List Box node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-list-boxes.html#navigating-to-page-nodes-from-a-grid-list-box-node "Link to this heading")
Note
The Page and Page Host nodes are deprecated. Use the Activity and Activity Host nodes to build navigable UIs for your application. See [Activities](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/activities/activities.html).
Use an alias when you want to navigate to a Page node from a node that is inside a list box node. For example, if you use a Grid List Box or a Trajectory List Box 3D node to create an address book and want to show the content of an address book entry in a Page node.
To navigate to Page nodes from a list box node:
  1. In the Node Tree press `Alt` and right-click each Page node to which you want to navigate to and select Alias. Kanzi Studio creates an alias that points to the node from which you created it, and places the alias to the nearest resource dictionary.
![../../_images/create-alias.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-alias.png)
  2. In the Dictionaries make sure that the aliases you created are in the resource dictionary that the list box node can access.
For example, place all aliases to the resource dictionary of the Screen node, or create a resource dictionary in the list box node and place the aliases to that resource dictionary. See [Using resource dictionaries](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/resources/using-resource-dictionaries.html).
![../../_images/aliases-in-context-resources.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/aliases-in-context-resources.png)
  3. Add and set the Navigate to Page action:
    1. In the Node Tree in the list box node select the node that contains the trigger that you want to use to navigate to one of the Page nodes for which you created the alias in the first step.
![../../_images/select-button.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/select-button.png)
    2. In the Node Components > Triggers press `Alt` and right-click the trigger that you want to use to navigate to the Page node, and create a Navigate to Page action.
![../../_images/add-navigate-to-page-action.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-navigate-to-page-action.png)
    3. In the Navigate to Page action set the Target Item property to the alias of the Page node to which you want to navigate.
All aliases start with a # sign.
![../../_images/navigate-to-car-page.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/navigate-to-car-page.png)


In the Preview when you click the node that contains the Navigate to Page action, you activate the Page node selected in the action.
## Reacting when the user interacts with a Grid List Box node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-list-boxes.html#reacting-when-the-user-interacts-with-a-grid-list-box-node "Link to this heading")
Use the List Box triggers to react when the user interacts with a Grid List Box node. For example, you can set the appearance of a Grid List Box node when the user scrolls that node.
You can use these List Box triggers with the Grid List Box nodes:  
| Name  | Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
| List Box: Item Loaded  |  List Box: Item Loaded trigger is set off when an item in a list box is created and loaded to the working memory. To set how many items around the visible items you want to keep loaded in the working memory at a time, use the Keep Alive Item Count property.  |  
| List Box: Item Selected  | List Box: Item Selected trigger is set off when the user selects an item in a list box.  |  
| List Box: Item Unloaded  |  List Box: Item Unloaded trigger is set off when an item in a list box is unloaded from the working memory. To set how many items around the visible items you want to keep loaded in the working memory at a time, use the Keep Alive Item Count property.  |  
| List Box: Scroll Finished  | List Box: Scroll Finished trigger is set off when the scrolling of a list box ends.  |  
| List Box: Scroll Started  | List Box: Scroll Started trigger is set off when the scrolling of a list box starts.  |  
| List Box: Scrolled  | List Box: Scrolled trigger is set of whenever a list box scrolls.  |  
| List Box: Target Changed  |  List Box: Target Changed trigger is set off when the scroll target of a list box changes. For example, the scroll target changes when the user selects a list box item and the list box scrolls to bring that item to the center of the list box area.  |  
| List Box: User Scroll Finished  | List Box: User Scroll Finished trigger is set off when the user stops scrolling a list box.  |  
| List Box: User Scroll Started  | List Box: User Scroll Started trigger is set off when the user starts to scroll a list box.  |  
To use the List Box triggers with a Grid List Box node:
  1. Create a Grid List Box node and add items to it. See [Creating a Grid List Box node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-list-boxes.html#creating-glb).
For example, create a Grid List Box 2D node.
![../../_images/create-grid-list-box-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-grid-list-box-2d.png) ![../../_images/contact-items-added.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/contact-items-added.png) ![../../_images/grid-list-box-2d-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/grid-list-box-2d-in-preview.png)
  2. Define the behavior that you want to set with the List Box triggers.
For example, create a state manager where you define the states which set the appearance of the Grid List Box 2D node when the Scroll Started and Scroll Finished triggers are set off. See [Creating a state manager](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/state-managers/using-state-managers.html#creating-a-state-manager).
  3. Add and configure a List Box trigger:
    1. In the Node Tree select the List Box node to which you want to add the trigger, and in the Node Components > Triggers add one of the List Box triggers.
For example, in the Node Tree select the Grid List Box node which you created in the beginning of this procedure, in the Node Components press `Alt` and right-click Triggers, and select Message Trigger > List Box > Scroll Started.
![../../_images/add-list-box-scroll-started-trigger.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-list-box-scroll-started-trigger.png)
    2. In the Node Components press `Alt` and right-click the trigger that you created in the previous step, select an action, and configure it.
For example, select the State Manager: Go to State action and in the action set the State property to the state which sets the appearance of the Grid List Box node when the List Box: Scroll Started trigger is set off.
![../../_images/list-box-scroll-started-add-go-to-state-action.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/list-box-scroll-started-add-go-to-state-action.png) ![../../_images/go-to-state-action-for-list-box-scroll-started.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/go-to-state-action-for-list-box-scroll-started.png)
  4. Repeat the previous step to add and configure more List Box triggers.
For example, add the List Box: Scroll Finished trigger. In the State Manager: Go to State action of the trigger set State to the state which sets the appearance of the node when that trigger is set off.


In the Preview when you scroll the Grid List Box node you created, the triggers you added are set off.
## Enabling the double-click gesture for Grid List Box items[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-list-boxes.html#enabling-the-double-click-gesture-for-grid-list-box-items "Link to this heading")
When you add to a List Box node items that support the double-click gesture, you must enable the double-click gesture for those items in the List Box Item Container prefab.
To learn how to enable the double-click gesture for a node, see [Enabling the multi-click gesture for a node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/multi-click-manipulator.html#enabling-the-multi-click-gesture-for-a-node).
To enable the double-click gesture for List Box items:
  1. Create a List Box Item Container prefab and set it as the Item Container Template of the List Box node. See [Creating a List Box Item Container prefab](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/container-controls/using-list-box-item-containers.html#create-list-box-item-container).
  2. In the Prefabs, select the List Box Item Container prefab. In the Properties, add and enable the Input > Double-Click Enabled property.
When you enable the Double-Click Enabled property, Kanzi installs in the List Box Item Container prefab a multi-click manipulator that generates double-click messages.
![../../_images/double-click-enabled.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/double-click-enabled.png)


## Scrolling a Grid List Box node with a slider[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-list-boxes.html#scrolling-a-grid-list-box-node-with-a-slider "Link to this heading")
You can use a Slider node to scroll a Grid List Box node. In this example you use a slider to scroll a vertical contacts list.
To use a slider to scroll a Grid List Box node:
  1. Create the Grid List Box node that you want to scroll.
For example:
    1. In the Node Tree create a Stack Layout 2D node.
![../../_images/stack-layout.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/stack-layout.png)
    2. From the Asset Packages > Factory Content drag the Contact List to the Node Tree and drop it on the Stack Layout 2D node. See [Factory Content assets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html).
![../../_images/asset-packages-fc-contact-list.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/asset-packages-fc-contact-list.png) ![../../_images/contact-list-instance.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/contact-list-instance.png)
  2. Create the Slider node that you use to scroll the Grid List Box node, and set the size and orientation of the Slider node to match those of the Grid List Box node.
For example:
    1. From the Asset Packages > Factory Content drag the Slider to the Node Tree and drop it on the Stack Layout 2D node.
![../../_images/asset-packages-fc-slider.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/asset-packages-fc-slider.png) ![../../_images/slider-instance.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/slider-instance.png) ![../../_images/contact-list-and-slider-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/contact-list-and-slider-in-preview.png)
    2. In the Node Tree select the Slider node, in the Properties click + Add Binding, and in the Binding Editor set:
       * Property to Layout Width
       * Expression to

```
{@../Contact List/Node.Height}

```
Copy to clipboard
This way you make the length of the slider rail match the height of the Contact List node.
Tip
You can start creating a binding for a property by right-clicking a property and selecting Create Binding.
This way you automatically add the property to the Binding Editor.
![../../_images/properties-create-binding.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-create-binding.png)
![../../_images/slider-layout-width-binding.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/slider-layout-width-binding.png)
    3. In the Properties add the Transform 2D > Layout Transformation property and set the Rotation property field to 90.
This way you make the slider vertical.
![../../_images/slider-rotation.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/slider-rotation.png) ![../../_images/slider-vertical-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/slider-vertical-in-preview.png)
    4. In the Properties click + Add Binding and in the Binding Editor set:
       * Property to Maximum Value
       * Expression to

```
# Get the number of items in the Contact List node.
itemCount = {@../Contact List/ListBoxConcept.ItemCount}

# Get the height of a cell that hosts a contact item in the Contact List node.
itemHeight = {@../Contact List/GridListBoxConcept.CellHeight}

# Get the height of the Contact List node.
listBoxHeight = {@../Contact List/Node.Height}

# Return the height of the invisible area of the Contact List node.
itemCount * itemHeight - listBoxHeight

```
Copy to clipboard
You bind the highest value of the Slider node to the height of the invisible area of the Contact List node. The lowest value of the Slider node is by default 0. This way you set the range of values in the slider to match the length of the contacts list.
![../../_images/slider-maximum-value-binding.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/slider-maximum-value-binding.png)
  3. In the Node Tree select the Slider node, in the Properties click + Add Binding, and in the Binding Editor set:
     * Binding Mode to Two way
     * Property to Value
     * Source to the Scroll Position property X or Y property field of the Grid List Box node that you want to scroll.
For example, set it to:

```
{@../Contact List/GridListBoxConcept.ScrollPosition}.Y

```
Copy to clipboard
You bind the Value property of the Slider node to the Scroll Position property Y property field of the Contact List node. This way you create a two-way connection between the position of the slider knob and the vertical scroll position of the list box.
![../../_images/slider-value-binding.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/slider-value-binding.png)


In the Preview when you move the slider knob, the contacts list scrolls, and when you scroll the contacts list, the slider knob moves.
![../../_images/slider-scroll-list-box.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/slider-scroll-list-box.gif)
## Controlling whether a Grid List Box node is in use[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-list-boxes.html#controlling-whether-a-grid-list-box-node-is-in-use "Link to this heading")
To control whether a Grid List Box node is in use, use the Input > Enabled property. A disabled Grid List Box node does not react to user input. When you disable a Grid List Box node, Kanzi stops ongoing gestures and preserves the selected item and scroll position of that Grid List Box node.
When you disable the Enabled property of a node, you effectively disable that node and its descendant nodes in the same overlay focus scope.
To observe whether a node is effectively enabled, use the Input > Effectively Enabled property in a state manager or a binding. For example, to visually indicate to the user whether a node is in use, create a state manager and use the Effectively Enabled property as its controller property.
See [Controlling how a node reacts to input](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/handling-input.html#controlling-how-a-node-reacts-to-input).
## Setting the appearance of a Grid List Box 2D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-list-boxes.html#setting-the-appearance-of-a-grid-list-box-2d-node "Link to this heading")
To set the appearance of 2D nodes:
  * You can fill 2D nodes with a solid color, a texture, or a material. See [Adjusting the appearance of 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/adjusting-the-appearance.html).
![../../_images/color-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/color-brush.png) ![../../_images/texture-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/texture-brush.png) ![../../_images/material-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/material-brush.png)
  * You can apply a post-processing effect to a 2D node. See [Effects for 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/2d-effects.html).
![../../_images/blur-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blur-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/mask-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mask-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/outline-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/outline-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/shadow-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/shadow-effect-2d.png)
  * You can rotate a 2D node around all three axes to create a 3D perspective effect. See [Creating a 3D perspective effect for 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/setting-the-perspective.html).
![../../_images/perspective-transformation-visualization.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/perspective-transformation-visualization.png)
  * You can apply custom rendering to 2D nodes to create post-processing effects. See [Applying custom rendering to 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/applying-custom-rendering.html).
![../../_images/texture-grayscale.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/texture-grayscale.png)
  * You can render a 2D node as pixel-perfect. See [Rendering pixel-perfect 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/adjusting-the-appearance.html#rendering-pixel-perfect-2d-nodes).
![../../_images/snap-to-pixel-icon.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/snap-to-pixel-icon.png)


## Using the Grid List Box 3D node in the API[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-list-boxes.html#using-the-grid-list-box-3d-node-in-the-api "Link to this heading")
To create a Grid List Box 3D node:

```
// Create a Grid List Box 3D named MyListBox.
GridListBox3DSharedPtr gridListBox = GridListBox3D::create(domain, "MyListBox");

```
Copy to clipboard
To configure the grid area:

```
// Make each grid cell be a 1x1x1 cube.
gridListBox->setCellWidth(1.0f);
gridListBox->setCellHeight(1.0f);
gridListBox->setDepth(1.0f);
// Make the grid contain three rows that are filled column by column.
gridListBox->setHeight(3.0f);
gridListBox->setDirection(GridListBoxConcept::GridDirectionDown);
// Make the grid contain 10 columns. Items that are dragged beyond these columns are made invisible.
gridListBox->setWidth(10.0f);
// Change the resting position when the list is scrolled to the beginning or end, so that items are not right at the grid edge.
gridListBox->setItemAreaBegin(0.2f);
gridListBox->setItemAreaEnd(0.8f);

```
Copy to clipboard
To add items to the list box:

```
// Create cube meshes and add them as items of the list box.
// Items on the grid appear in the order you add them to the list.
Model3DSharedPtr item1 = Model3D::createCube(domain, "item1", 1.0f, ThemeRed);
Model3DSharedPtr item2 = Model3D::createCube(domain, "item2", 1.0f, ThemeGreen);
Model3DSharedPtr item3 = Model3D::createCube(domain, "item3", 1.0f, ThemeBlue);
Model3DSharedPtr item4 = Model3D::createCube(domain, "item4", 1.0f, ThemeOrange);
Model3DSharedPtr item5 = Model3D::createCube(domain, "item5", 1.0f, ThemeYellow);
gridListBox->addItem(item1);
gridListBox->addItem(item2);
gridListBox->addItem(item3);
gridListBox->addItem(item4);
gridListBox->addItem(item5);

```
Copy to clipboard
For details, see the `GridListBox3D[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a18682.html)` class.
## Using the Grid List Box 2D node in the API[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-list-boxes.html#using-the-grid-list-box-2d-node-in-the-api "Link to this heading")
To create a Grid List Box 2D node:

```
// Create a Grid List Box 2D named MyListBox.
GridListBox2DSharedPtr gridListBox = GridListBox2D::create(domain, "MyListBox");

```
Copy to clipboard
To configure the grid area:

```
// Make each grid cell be a 100x100 square.
gridListBox->setCellWidth(100.0f);
gridListBox->setCellHeight(100.0f);
// Make the grid contain three rows that are filled column by column.
gridListBox->setHeight(300.0f);
gridListBox->setDirection(GridListBoxConcept::GridDirectionDown);
// Make the grid contain 10 columns. Items that are dragged beyond these columns are made invisible.
gridListBox->setWidth(1000.0f);
// Change the resting position when the list is scrolled to the beginning or end, so that items are not right at the grid edge.
gridListBox->setItemAreaBegin(0.2f);
gridListBox->setItemAreaEnd(0.8f);

```
Copy to clipboard
To add items to the list box:

```
// Create images and add them as items of the list box.
// Items on the grid appear in the order you add them to the list.
for (int i = 0; i < 5; ++i)
{
    Image2DSharedPtr item = Image2D::create(domain, "item" + to_string(i));
    item->setImage(item->acquireResource<Texture>(ResourceID("DefaultTexture")));
    // Make the images shrink to the cell size.
    item->setHorizontalAlignment(Node::HorizontalAlignmentStretch);
    item->setVerticalAlignment(Node::VerticalAlignmentStretch);
    gridListBox->addItem(item);
}

```
Copy to clipboard
For details, see the `GridListBox2D[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a18678.html)` class.
##  Grid List Box property types and messages[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-list-boxes.html#grid-list-box-property-types-and-messages "Link to this heading")
For lists of the available property types and messages for the Grid List Box nodes, see [Grid List Box 2D](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/node-and-resource-reference/grid-list-box-2d-reference.html) and [Grid List Box 3D](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/node-and-resource-reference/grid-list-box-3d-reference.html).
## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-list-boxes.html#sa "Link to this heading")

# Using the Trajectory List Box 3D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html#using-the-trajectory-list-box-3d-node "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Use the Trajectory List Box 3D node to create scrollable lists of items arranged along a trajectory in 3D space.
![../../_images/trajectory-list-box-3d.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-list-box-3d.gif)
Kanzi Studio comes with several types of trajectories. When you need a different type of trajectory, create a spline trajectory in a third-party tool and import it to your Kanzi Studio project. See [Trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/trajectories.html).
The items in a Trajectory List Box 3D node appear in the order that you add them to the Trajectory List Box 3D node. To select an item in a Trajectory List Box 3D node, click or tap that item.
The size of the trajectory defines the interactive area for click and drag gestures. If the trajectory is too small, the user is not able to select the items in the Trajectory List Box 3D node. To avoid this, make sure that the trajectory is large enough. See [Trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/trajectories.html).
The Trajectory List Box 3D nodes that you create in Kanzi Studio are focus scopes and handle the key focus and key input by default. See [Handling the key focus in a List Box node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/container-controls/list-box-nodes.html#lb-handling-key-focus).
Note
Items in all list box nodes (Grid List Box nodes and Trajectory List Box 3D node) are not its child nodes, even though in Kanzi Studio it seems so when you add items to a list box. Because list box items are not child nodes of a list box, you cannot refer to these items from outside of a list box using paths or aliases. If you need to refer from a list box item to an object outside of a list box, use bindings and aliases. See [Binding to properties outside of a Grid List Box node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-list-boxes.html#binding) and [Navigating to Page nodes from a Trajectory List Box 3D node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html#navigating).
Trajectory List Box 3D node is an interactive version of the Trajectory Layout 3D node. See [Using the Trajectory Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html).
For an example of how to use the Trajectory List Box 3D node to create an interactive scrollable list of items, see the [Trajectory list box example](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html#trajecto).
## Creating a Trajectory List Box 3D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html#creating-a-trajectory-list-box-3d-node "Link to this heading")
To create a Trajectory List Box 3D node:
  1. In the Node Tree, press `Alt` and right-click the 3D node where you want to create a Trajectory List Box 3D node and select Trajectory List Box 3D.
For example, create a Trajectory List Box 3D node in the Scene node.
![../../_images/create-trajectory-list-box-3d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-trajectory-list-box-3d.png)
Tip
To see the trajectory, in the Preview click ![image-analyze-off](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/analyze-off.png) to enter the Analyze mode, right-click ![image-analyze-on](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/analyze-on.png), and select Debug objects.
![../../_images/visualize-mode-debug-objects.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/visualize-mode-debug-objects.png)
  2. In the Node Tree, add items to the Trajectory List Box 3D node.
Use a data source to add items to a List Box node. See [Using a data source](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/data-sources/using-a-data-source.html).
For example, to create an album list, add several nodes that represent the albums in the list. See [Using the List Box Item Container prefabs](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/container-controls/using-list-box-item-containers.html).
As you add items, the Trajectory List Box 3D node arranges them along the trajectory used by the Trajectory List Box 3D node.
To browse the items in a Trajectory List Box 3D node, in the Preview, click and drag the items in the Trajectory List Box 3D node.
![../../_images/trajectory-list-box-3d-add-item.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-list-box-3d-add-item.png) ![../../_images/trajectory-list-box-3d-with-items-in-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-list-box-3d-with-items-in-project.png) ![../../_images/trajectory-list-box-with-items-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-list-box-with-items-in-preview.png)
  3. (Optional)
Kanzi Studio creates and uses a circle trajectory by default. You can use an angle, arc, circle, ellipse, line, rectangle, spiral, spline, or a trapezoid trajectory. See [Trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/trajectories.html).


## Fine-tuning the mechanics of a Trajectory List Box 3D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html#fine-tuning-the-mechanics-of-a-trajectory-list-box-3d-node "Link to this heading")
You can fine-tune the mechanics of a Trajectory List Box 3D node. You can set the list box to:
  * **Bring the selected item to the center of the list box.**
To set the list box to bring the item to the center of the list box object when the user clicks that item, set the Selection Behavior property to Bring Center. Use the Cursor Offset property to set the direction in which selection moves the items in the list box. Use the Cursor Offset property to set the direction in which selection moves the items in the list box.
![../../_images/selection-behavior.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/selection-behavior.gif)
  * **Show items from the beginning after reaching the last item.**
To start showing the items in a Trajectory List Box 3D from the beginning after reaching the last item, enable the Looping property.
![../../_images/loop-along-x.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/loop-along-x.gif)
  * **Use either x or y axis for scrolling the items in the list box.**
To set the scrolling axis, set the Allowed Scroll Axis property.
For example, to set the list box so that the user can scroll along the y axis to browse the items, set the Allowed Scroll Axis property to Y axis.
  * **Reverse the scrolling direction.**
To reverse the direction in which the list box scrolls when the user clicks and drags the items, add and enable the Reversed Scrolling property.
  * **Change the appearance of the items based on their location on the trajectory.**
To set how the items look at different points on the trajectory, use the Item Area Begin and Item Area End properties. You use the Item Area Begin and Item Area End properties to set the value of the Visible Amount In Parent property, which sets shaders to change the appearance of an item based on the location of that object in the list box.
For example, if you use the Visible Amount In Parent property to gradually change the visibility of an item, set the Item Area Begin property to a larger value and the Item Area End property to a smaller value. This way you limit the area where that item is visible.


## Nesting Trajectory List Box 3D nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html#nesting-trajectory-list-box-3d-nodes "Link to this heading")
You can nest Trajectory List Box 3D nodes to create a Trajectory List Box 3D node within a Trajectory List Box 3D node, each of which you can scroll independently. For example, you can create a Trajectory List Box 3D which you use to scroll on a circle trajectory Trajectory Layout 3D nodes which contain sets of albums.
In a Trajectory List Box 3D node, use the Allowed Scroll Axis property to set the axis on which the user can scroll the list.
To nest Trajectory List Box 3D nodes:
  1. Create a Trajectory List Box 3D node. See [Creating a Trajectory List Box 3D node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html#creating-tlb-3d-node).
For example, use the circle trajectory to create a path in the shape of a circle. See [Using circle trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-circle-trajectories.html).
![../../_images/create-trajectory-list-box-3d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-trajectory-list-box-3d.png) ![../../_images/circle-trajectory-for-nested.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/circle-trajectory-for-nested.png)
  2. Select the Trajectory List Box 3D node that you created in the previous step. In the Properties, set the Allowed Scroll Axis property to the axis on which you want that node to scroll.
For example, to set the Trajectory List Box 3D node to scroll on the x axis, set the Allowed Scroll Axis property to X axis.
![../../_images/use-circle-trajectory.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/use-circle-trajectory.png)
  3. Create the Trajectory List Box 3D node that you want to nest in the Trajectory List Box 3D node that you created in the previous step.
For example, if you want to create several nested Trajectory List Box 3D nodes of albums:
    1. In the Prefabs, create a Trajectory List Box 3D node.
The Trajectory List Box 3D node arranges its items along a circle trajectory by default.
    2. In the Properties, set the Allowed Scroll Axis property to X axis.
![../../_images/trajectory-list-box-prefab.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-list-box-prefab.png) ![../../_images/use-circle-trajectory.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/use-circle-trajectory.png)
  4. In the Node Tree, add items to the Trajectory List Box 3D node.
For example, from the Prefabs, drag several Trajectory List Box 3D prefabs that represent the album lists. In each nested Trajectory List Box 3D node, add items that represent the albums in each list.
You can add items to a Trajectory List Box 3D using a data source. See [Using a data source](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/data-sources/using-a-data-source.html).
![../../_images/items-in-nested-trajectory-list-box.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/items-in-nested-trajectory-list-box.png)


## Binding to properties outside of a Trajectory List Box 3D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html#binding-to-properties-outside-of-a-trajectory-list-box-3d-node "Link to this heading")
Use an alias when you want to bind a property of a list box item to a property of a node outside of the list box.
For example, if you have a Grid List Box 3D or a Trajectory List Box 3D node with a Text Block 3D node item and want to set the Text property value of the Text Block 3D node to a value of an Empty Node 3D node property that is not in the list box:
![../../_images/binding-outside-a-list-box---structure.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/binding-outside-a-list-box---structure.png)
  1. In the Node Tree press `Alt` and right-click the nodes that contain the property to which you want to bind and select Alias. See [Using aliases](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/aliases/using-aliases.html).
For example, create an alias for the Empty Node 3D node.
  2. In the Dictionaries make sure that the aliases you created are in the resource dictionary that the list box node can access.
For example, place all aliases to the resource dictionary of the Screen node, or create a resource dictionary in the list box node and place the aliases to that resource dictionary. See [Using resource dictionaries](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/resources/using-resource-dictionaries.html).
  3. Create the binding:
    1. In the Node Tree select the node inside the list box node from which you want to bind to a node outside of the list box node.
    2. In the Properties click + Add Binding and create the binding using the alias to bind to the property in a node outside of the list box node.
For example, in the Text Block 3D node create a binding to the Empty Node 3D node using the alias you created in the first step. See [Bindings expressions reference](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/reference-for-bindings-expressions.html).
For example, use this binding expression:

```
{#Empty Node 3D/TextConcept.Text}

```
Copy to clipboard
The Text property in the Text Block 3D node gets the value of the Text property from the Empty Node 3D node.
    3. Click Save.


## Navigating to Page nodes from a Trajectory List Box 3D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html#navigating-to-page-nodes-from-a-trajectory-list-box-3d-node "Link to this heading")
Note
The Page and Page Host nodes are deprecated. Use the Activity and Activity Host nodes to build navigable UIs for your application. See [Activities](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/activities/activities.html).
Use an alias when you want to navigate to a Page node from a node that is inside a list box node. For example, if you use a Grid List Box or a Trajectory List Box 3D node to create an address book and want to show the content of an address book entry in a Page node.
To navigate to Page nodes from a list box node:
  1. In the Node Tree press `Alt` and right-click each Page node to which you want to navigate to and select Alias. Kanzi Studio creates an alias that points to the node from which you created it, and places the alias to the nearest resource dictionary.
![../../_images/create-alias.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-alias.png)
  2. In the Dictionaries make sure that the aliases you created are in the resource dictionary that the list box node can access.
For example, place all aliases to the resource dictionary of the Screen node, or create a resource dictionary in the list box node and place the aliases to that resource dictionary. See [Using resource dictionaries](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/resources/using-resource-dictionaries.html).
![../../_images/aliases-in-context-resources.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/aliases-in-context-resources.png)
  3. Add and set the Navigate to Page action:
    1. In the Node Tree in the list box node select the node that contains the trigger that you want to use to navigate to one of the Page nodes for which you created the alias in the first step.
![../../_images/select-button.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/select-button.png)
    2. In the Node Components > Triggers press `Alt` and right-click the trigger that you want to use to navigate to the Page node, and create a Navigate to Page action.
![../../_images/add-navigate-to-page-action.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-navigate-to-page-action.png)
    3. In the Navigate to Page action set the Target Item property to the alias of the Page node to which you want to navigate.
All aliases start with a # sign.
![../../_images/navigate-to-car-page.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/navigate-to-car-page.png)


In the Preview when you click the node that contains the Navigate to Page action, you activate the Page node selected in the action.
## Reacting when the user interacts with a Trajectory List Box 3D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html#reacting-when-the-user-interacts-with-a-trajectory-list-box-3d-node "Link to this heading")
Use the List Box triggers to react when the user interacts with a Trajectory List Box 3D node. For example, you can set the appearance of a Trajectory List Box 3D when the user scrolls that list box.
You can use these List Box triggers with a Trajectory List Box 3D node:  
| Name  | Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
| List Box: Item Loaded  |  List Box: Item Loaded trigger is set off when an item in a list box is created and loaded to the working memory. To set how many items around the visible items you want to keep loaded in the working memory at a time, use the Keep Alive Item Count property.  |  
| List Box: Item Selected  | List Box: Item Selected trigger is set off when the user selects an item in a list box.  |  
| List Box: Item Unloaded  |  List Box: Item Unloaded trigger is set off when an item in a list box is unloaded from the working memory. To set how many items around the visible items you want to keep loaded in the working memory at a time, use the Keep Alive Item Count property.  |  
| List Box: Scroll Finished  | List Box: Scroll Finished trigger is set off when the scrolling of a list box ends.  |  
| List Box: Scroll Started  | List Box: Scroll Started trigger is set off when the scrolling of a list box starts.  |  
| List Box: Scrolled  | List Box: Scrolled trigger is set of whenever a list box scrolls.  |  
| List Box: Target Changed  |  List Box: Target Changed trigger is set off when the scroll target of a list box changes. For example, the scroll target changes when the user selects a list box item and the list box scrolls to bring that item to the center of the list box area.  |  
| List Box: User Scroll Finished  | List Box: User Scroll Finished trigger is set off when the user stops scrolling a list box.  |  
| List Box: User Scroll Started  | List Box: User Scroll Started trigger is set off when the user starts to scroll a list box.  |  
To use the List Box triggers with a Trajectory List Box 3D node:
  1. Create a Trajectory List Box 3D node and add items to it. See [Creating a Trajectory List Box 3D node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html#creating-tlb-3d-node).
![../../_images/trajectory-list-box-3d-with-items-in-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-list-box-3d-with-items-in-project.png) ![../../_images/trajectory-list-box-with-items-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-list-box-with-items-in-preview.png)
  2. Define the behavior that you want to set with the List Box triggers.
For example, create a state manager where you define the states which set the appearance of the Trajectory List Box 3D node when the List Box: Scroll Started and List Box: Scroll Finished triggers are set off. See [Creating a state manager](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/state-managers/using-state-managers.html#creating-a-state-manager).
  3. Add and configure a List Box trigger:
    1. In the Node Tree, select the List Box node to which you want to add the trigger. In the Node Components > Triggers, create one of the List Box triggers.
For example, in the Node Tree, select the Trajectory List Box 3D node that you created in the beginning of this procedure. In the Node Components, press `Alt` and right-click Triggers, and select Message Trigger > List Box > Scroll Started.
![../../_images/add-list-box-scroll-started-trigger.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-list-box-scroll-started-trigger.png)
    2. In the Node Components, press `Alt` and right-click the trigger that you created in the previous step, select an action, and configure it.
For example, select the State Manager: Go to State action. In the action, set the State property to the state that sets the appearance of the Trajectory List Box 3D node when the List Box: Scroll Started trigger is set off.
![../../_images/list-box-scroll-started-add-go-to-state-action.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/list-box-scroll-started-add-go-to-state-action.png) ![../../_images/trajectory-list-box-go-to-state-action.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-list-box-go-to-state-action.png)
  4. Repeat the previous step to add and configure more List Box triggers.
For example, add the List Box: Scroll Finished trigger. In the State Manager: Go to State action of the trigger, set State to the state that sets the appearance of the node when that trigger is set off.


In the Preview, when you scroll the Trajectory List Box 3D node that you created, the triggers you added are set off.
## Controlling whether a Trajectory List Box 3D node is in use[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html#controlling-whether-a-trajectory-list-box-3d-node-is-in-use "Link to this heading")
To control whether a Trajectory List Box 3D node is in use, use the Input > Enabled property. A disabled Trajectory List Box 3D node does not react to user input. When you disable a Trajectory List Box 3D node, Kanzi stops ongoing gestures and preserves the selected item and scroll position of that Trajectory List Box 3D node.
When you disable the Enabled property of a node, you effectively disable that node and its descendant nodes in the same overlay focus scope.
To observe whether a node is effectively enabled, use the Input > Effectively Enabled property in a state manager or a binding. For example, to visually indicate to the user whether a node is in use, create a state manager and use the Effectively Enabled property as its controller property.
See [Controlling how a node reacts to input](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/handling-input.html#controlling-how-a-node-reacts-to-input).
## Enabling the double-click gesture for Trajectory List Box items[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html#enabling-the-double-click-gesture-for-trajectory-list-box-items "Link to this heading")
When you add to a List Box node items that support the double-click gesture, you must enable the double-click gesture for those items in the List Box Item Container prefab.
To learn how to enable the double-click gesture for a node, see [Enabling the multi-click gesture for a node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/multi-click-manipulator.html#enabling-the-multi-click-gesture-for-a-node).
To enable the double-click gesture for List Box items:
  1. Create a List Box Item Container prefab and set it as the Item Container Template of the List Box node. See [Creating a List Box Item Container prefab](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/container-controls/using-list-box-item-containers.html#create-list-box-item-container).
  2. In the Prefabs, select the List Box Item Container prefab. In the Properties, add and enable the Input > Double-Click Enabled property.
When you enable the Double-Click Enabled property, Kanzi installs in the List Box Item Container prefab a multi-click manipulator that generates double-click messages.
![../../_images/double-click-enabled.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/double-click-enabled.png)


## Trajectory list box example[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html#trajectory-list-box-example "Link to this heading")
This example shows the use of the Trajectory List Box 3D node to create an interactive scrollable list of items. The example implements a simple gallery of photos with a selection effect using an animation.
The Trajectory List Box 3D node, its Circle Trajectory, content shown in the Trajectory List Box 3D, and animation that highlights the centered photo are created in Kanzi Studio. The point of time at which a highlight-animation is launched is defined based on the scroll speed and focused item data available from the user input events that the trajectory list box component produces.
The Trajectory List Box 3D node in the example uses these features:
  * Looping. You can clamp the items in the Trajectory List Box 3D node to the defined trajectory start and end or to transition between the start and end positions, as in this example, with the Looping property.
  * Trajectory. To use a trajectory for the Trajectory List Box 3D, you need to create it in the Library > Trajectories. You can create circle and line trajectories in Kanzi Studio. To use a spline trajectory, create a spline in a third-party tool, import it, and add the spline as a Spline Trajectory. See [Using circle trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-circle-trajectories.html), [Using line trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-line-trajectories.html), and [Using spline trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-spline-trajectories.html). You can customize the trajectory by adding and setting trajectory properties such as Item Area Begin, Item Area End, Cursor Offset, and Override Distance.
  * **Selection and target behavior**. Selection and target events are handled separately. The target changed message is generated at the moment the user releases the pointer. It contains the information on the item that is brought to the center with the current trajectory movement. The selection message is generated when a user selects an item by clicking or tapping it. You can select the Bring Center selection behavior in Kanzi Studio. You can define more actions for the target and selection events for any member of the Trajectory List Box 3D, or even the trajectory list box component itself, by setting invoked actions for List Box: Target Changed or List Box: Item Selected triggers.


### Getting the example[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html#getting-the-example "Link to this heading")
To get the example, in the Kanzi Studio Quick Start window, click Projects and select the Examples tab. Next to the Trajectory_list_box example, click ![download](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/download.svg).
Kanzi Studio downloads the example to the `<KanziWorkspace>/Examples/Trajectory_list_box` directory.
## Using the Trajectory List Box 3D node in the API[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html#using-the-trajectory-list-box-3d-node-in-the-api "Link to this heading")
To create a Trajectory List Box 3D node:

```
// Create a Trajectory List Box 3D named MyListBox.
TrajectoryListBox3DSharedPtr trajectoryListBox = TrajectoryListBox3D::create(domain, "MyListBox");

```
Copy to clipboard
To set the trajectory that you want the Trajectory List Box 3D node to use:

```
// Create a circle trajectory named Circle with radius of 4 device independent units.
TrajectorySharedPtr trajectory = Trajectory::createCircle(Vector3(), Vector3::positiveY(), 0.0f, 4.0f, domain, "Circle");

// Set the list box to use the trajectory.
trajectoryListBox->setTrajectory(trajectory);
// Increase the layout size to cover the whole trajectory.
trajectoryListBox->setWidth(10.0f);
trajectoryListBox->setDepth(10.0f);
trajectoryListBox->setHeight(3.0f);

```
Copy to clipboard
To add items to the Trajectory List Box 3D node:

```
// Create cube meshes and add them as items of the Trajectory List Box 3D node.
// Items on the trajectory appear in the order that you add them to the Trajectory List Box 3D node.
Model3DSharedPtr item1 = Model3D::createCube(domain, "item1", 1.0f, ThemeRed);
Model3DSharedPtr item2 = Model3D::createCube(domain, "item2", 1.0f, ThemeGreen);
Model3DSharedPtr item3 = Model3D::createCube(domain, "item3", 1.0f, ThemeBlue);
Model3DSharedPtr item4 = Model3D::createCube(domain, "item4", 1.0f, ThemeOrange);
Model3DSharedPtr item5 = Model3D::createCube(domain, "item5", 1.0f, ThemeYellow);
trajectoryListBox->addItem(item1);
trajectoryListBox->addItem(item2);
trajectoryListBox->addItem(item3);
trajectoryListBox->addItem(item4);
trajectoryListBox->addItem(item5);

```
Copy to clipboard
To make the Trajectory List Box 3D node loop its items:

```
// Make the Trajectory List Box 3D node to loop. All items fit to the trajectory so that they are positioned evenly.
trajectoryListBox->setLooping(true);

```
Copy to clipboard
To set how the Trajectory List Box 3D node reacts to items selection:

```
// Make clicking items bring them to the center of the trajectory.
trajectoryListBox->setSelectionBehavior(ListBoxConcept::SelectionBehaviorBringToCenter);
// Change the position where the clicked items are brought to be one quarter from the beginning of the trajectory.
trajectoryListBox->setCursorOffset(0.25f);

```
Copy to clipboard
For details, see the `TrajectoryListBox3D[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a18898.html)` class.
##  Trajectory List Box 3D property types[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html#trajectory-list-box-3d-property-types "Link to this heading")
For a list of the available property types for the Trajectory List Box 3D node, see [Trajectory List Box 3D](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/node-and-resource-reference/trajectory-list-box-3d-reference.html).
## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html#sa "Link to this heading")
[Using the Grid List Box nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-list-boxes.html)
[Using the Trajectory Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html)
[Using angle trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-angle-trajectories.html)
[Using arc trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-arc-trajectories.html)
[Using circle trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-circle-trajectories.html)
[Using ellipse trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-ellipse-trajectories.html)
[Using line trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-line-trajectories.html)
[Using rectangle trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-rectangle-trajectories.html)
[Using spiral trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-spiral-trajectories.html)
[Using spline trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-spline-trajectories.html)
